findings.title: Compile ordinary macro forms containing caller-owned function and Var constants
findings.description: The public Runtime path sends ordinary eval forms to the isolated Macro service, including authenticated NativeConstant nodes for current functions/Vars. A shipped when-let or an eval-defined passthrough macro tries to quote its explicit argument in that different Store and hits the correct owner guard. Consequently simple generated forms accepted by Clojure fail before compilation can finish. No captures, foreign references supplied by the user, reflection, or hidden internals are needed. The same-owner actual compiled Macro control succeeds, demonstrating host-dependent public behavior.

findings.title: Recheck live macro authorization after earlier expansion changes its root
findings.description: synchronize_evaluation_macros runs once before preparing a whole eval unit. Both expansion paths then trust Environment.source_macro_overridden from that snapshot. A caller-owned transformer can recursively eval an ordinary definition of its own Var, correctly clearing the actual macro flag. Later uses in the same vector still invoke it as a transformer. Re-reading the selected function each time does not refresh its authorization. This repeats expansion-time effects and changes a required ordinary runtime call into another macro expansion.

findings.title: Accept ordinary self-evaluating nominal values at the public eval boundary
findings.description: Evaluation decodes its argument through the strict macro-syntax whitelist before the scalar identity fast path. NativeRead only exempts functions, classes and Vars, so already supported ordinary Atom and Delay objects are rejected even at the top level. Clojure Compiler.eval returns these non-collection, non-symbol objects unchanged. The actual compiled Macro control fails identically, so this is not an unavoidable cross-Store transfer.

findings.title: Admit false or nil :macro metadata on ordinary evaluated definitions
findings.description: The definition admission check rejects the presence of any :macro key outside an internally authorized macro declaration, without inspecting its value. Thus eval cannot create an ordinary Var with :macro false or nil and inspect its metadata/isMacro result. Clojure retains the key/value and reports Boolean false. This is a pre-existing admission restriction, not a demonstrated false-value implementation mismatch, but the unchanged public eval/special-form and ordinary definition contract contains no waiver for it. The program uses only eval, def, meta, contains?, keyword lookup and the Var isMacro method already provided by this PR.
